To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lytF gene product is required for cell integrity at the restrictive temperature, that smhA1, smhB1 and smhA2, smhB2 are alleles of the same gene (smh), and that smh is required for the expression of lytF function.

(i) the temperature-sensitive lytF mutation confers a lytic phenotype at the restrictive temperature; (ii) this phenotype is suppressed by smhA1 or smhB1 mutations; and (iii) the smhA1, smhB1, murH, lyd and lytE mutations all belong to a gene group that includes the lytF gene.

(1) a new Eschericha coli gene designated lytF was isolated as a temperature-sensitive mutation that conferred lysis at the restrictive temperatur, (2) the lytF gene was shown to be located on the linkage map at 62. 5 min, (3) the lytE gene was shown to map at 25 min, and (4) the smhA and lytF genes were shown to be allelic.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation and characterization of temperature-sensitive mutants of E. coli that lyse at the restrictive temperature and with the identification of the genes that encode the temperature-sensitive products of these mutations.
the isolation and characterization of mutations in Escherichia Coli that cause bacteriolysis at restrictive temperatures.
the identification of new genes that are involved in the regulation of autolysis in Escherichia colii.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lytF, murH, lyts and lytE gene products are all required for the maintenance of normal cell wall structure, and that the lytE, lytD, lytF and murH genes are all required for cell wall turnover.
the smhA locus is a suppressor of the lytD locus and that the smhB locus is a suppresser of the lytE and lytF loci, all three loci being located at 25 min on the linkage m...
the murH, lyts and smh genes comprise a single group of functionally related genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the murH, lyts, lytE and lytF genes are related and may be functionally equivalent.
smhA1, smhB1 and lytF mutations all suppress the temperature sensitivity and lysis phenotypes of murH, lyts and lytF mutants and that smhA and lytF are allelic.
the smhA and the smhB genes are extragenic suppressor loci for a group of genes, including lytF, which are involved in the autolysis process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lytE, lytD, lytF and murH, although not allelic, may constitute an operon.

the lytF gene, which encodes a protein with an apparent molecular mass of 30,000, may be a new member of a group of genes that are required for the normal maintenance of the integrity of the cell envelope.
the smhA1 allele is an extragenic suppressor of a temperature-sensitive allele of lytF, which confers a lysis phenotype.
